title: You could’ve FaceTimed an Eel....
format: 9:16 short, 30 fps; green-screen talking head (creator bottom-left, ~45% frame height, red headband, holding a lav mic like a reporter) over stock/news footage of the topic; burned-in sentence captions top-centre; spoken VO. Originally a TikTok 'reply to comment' video reposted to Shorts.
transcript_source: YouTube auto-subs (en); full timestamped transcript at research/library/transcripts/Ky0XPonYDcc.txt

devices: second-person 'You could've' = missed-opportunity / FOMO framing: there was a window and you weren't told
absurd collision of modern tech verb (FaceTimed) with a weird animal (eel)
trailing ellipsis '....' signals deadpan disbelief, invites the click to resolve
no number, no question mark, under 6 words; reads like a text message, not a headline
title_pattern.notes: The title is the punchline of a real 2020 news story (Tokyo Sumida Aquarium's 'face-showing festival' for shy garden eels during COVID closure). Outlier because the story is true, absurd and wholesome; the title gives away the 'what' but not the 'why', so the click is for the why.

thumbnail.composition: Auto-frame from 0s (Shorts feed shows the first frame; the 16:9 jpg is the 9:16 frame pillarboxed with a blurred zoomed copy). Creator's head and shoulders occupy lower-left third in front of a vertical aquarium shot of spotted garden eels standing out of white sand; a TikTok 'Reply to comment' white speech bubble sits upper-centre.
thumbnail.text: 'THEY FACE TIMED THE EELS' + crying-laughing emoji, bold black caps in a white rounded comment bubble (the viewer comment being answered), ~1/12 frame height
thumbnail.colours: Teal/cyan aquarium water, cream sand and pale spotted eels, single red accent on the creator's headband, white bubble
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Human face at the same apparent size as a foreground eel standing beside him, so he looks like he is in the tank with them; dozens of small eels behind give depth
thumbnail.why_it_works: The comment bubble is social proof that someone else already found this hilarious, and it states the absurd fact in plain caps. The eels are visually strange (periscope-like stalks), so the frame reads as 'what am I looking at?' even before the text.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: Yeah, so I should probably explain the story. So obviously during COVID, people couldn't go to zoos...
hook.on_screen_0_2s: Reply-to-comment bubble: 'THEY FACE TIMED THE EELS' (emoji)
hook.device: Reply-to-comment cold open: the absurd payoff is stated first by a 'viewer' comment, then the narrator jumps in mid-conversation ('Yeah, so I should probably explain') as if answering a friend. Payoff-first + curiosity gap (why would anyone FaceTime an eel?) + casual mid-sentence start that skips any intro.

beats.summary: Comment bubble states the absurd fact ('they FaceTimed the eels'); narrator: 'I should probably explain the story'.
COVID closed zoos; animals used to seeing people started to miss them, including eels.
Spotted garden eels in a Japanese aquarium had 'bad social anxiety' and buried themselves in sand whenever people came near (anthropomorphised flaw).
Daily exposure to visitors made the eels get over their shyness, which helped scientists study them.
'But of course' zoos closed for COVID, eels forgot humans and went back to hiding whenever scientists approached.
'Which is how they got an idea': the zoo asked people to FaceTime the eels to remind them humans exist and cure their 'crippling social anxiety'.
'2020 had a lot of weird headlines, but a zoo asking people to FaceTime introverted eels in the name of science is definitely up there' over a goofy eel close-up; no CTA.

pacing.wpm_note: Very fast; VO likely sped up ~1.2-1.3x in edit (TikTok-native style). For TTS remake target ~220-250 wpm.
pacing.notes: Background changes only 7 times (cuts at 7.1, 13.3, 21.0, 26.7, 27.9, 35.1 s), but the sentence caption swaps every 2-6 s, so the screen is never static. Each background cut lands on a story turn ('Because', 'But eventually', 'But of course', 'Which is how', '2020...'). No music bed audible beyond VO; no SFX.

techniques_worth_copying: Payoff-first cold open via a fake/real viewer comment bubble stating the absurd fact, then 'let me explain' — the whole video becomes the answer to a question the viewer already has.
Anthropomorphise the animal with a relatable human diagnosis ('bad social anxiety', 'introverted', 'crippling anxiety', 'got over their shyness').

Tight 5-beat causal chain with spoken connectives as turn markers: 'Because' / 'But eventually' / 'which was good because' / 'But of course' / 'which is how they got an idea'. Each connective = a visual cut.
Status quo -> fix -> relapse -> absurd fix: the setback before the reveal makes the FaceTime idea land as a solution, not a random fact.
Wry button ending that zooms out to the year/era ('2020 had a lot of weird headlines, but...') instead of a CTA; ends on the funniest image (eel staring at camera).
One full-sentence caption at a time, top-centre, white text with soft shadow; long sentences allowed (up to 7 lines) because speech is so fast.
True, verifiable, wholesome-weird news story under 45 s; no tangents.

code_only_remake_needs.summary: Easy to remake in Remotion: swap the green-screen creator for a recurring SVG mascot/narrator in the lower-left and the stock footage for illustrated SVG scenes.
assets: Narrator mascot SVG (lower-left, ~40% height) with 3-4 mouth shapes for lip-flap synced to TTS amplitude, plus a prop (mic)
Illustrated SVG garden eels (spotted stalks) with a parametric 'rise/retract into sand' animation and sway; 30-60 instances for a colony
Aquarium tank scene (teal gradient water, light shafts, sand), empty-sand variant, and a 'tablets propped against glass showing cartoon faces' scene
Comment-bubble component (white rounded rect, 'Reply to @user's comment' small grey line, bold caps text, emoji) for the cold open
Hero close-up eel face with big goofy eyes for the final button
motion: Hard cuts between background scenes on each causal connective; optional subtle Ken Burns (1.0->1.05 scale) to compensate for the lack of live footage motion
Letterbox layout: black top band for captions, scene band mid-frame, mascot overlapping the bottom
Eel hide/emerge animation driven by story state (emerged when 'familiar', retracted when 'shy') — turns the narrative into a visible state change, which the original only gets from stock clips
code_only_remake_needs.captions: Sentence-level captions (not word-pop), white sans with shadow, centred top 20% of frame, changing every ~3 s, timed from TTS word timestamps
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Single fast TTS voice (~230-250 wpm, Kokoro), no music or a very quiet bed; optional pop SFX on the comment bubble
code_only_remake_needs.risk: The original's charm is the creator's deadpan face and real footage proving it happened; a code remake should add one 'proof' device (e.g. a stylised news-headline card with date) to keep the 'this is real' credibility.
